Summarise a cross-validation

Source: R/cross_validation.R
summary.RiskMap_cross_validation.Rd

Gives the average scores of each model over all test observations, their differences from a reference model, and the areas of the calibration curves.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap_cross_validation'
summary(object, reference = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

The result of assess_prediction().

reference

Optional name of the model that the others are compared with.

...

Not used, and an error if given, so that a misspelt argument is not ignored.

Value

A data frame of class summary.RiskMap_cross_validation with one row for each model, named after it, and the columns CRPS and SCRPS, PIT_area, PIT_area_expected and PIT_area_limit, and, when reference is given, CRPS_difference, CRPS_se, SCRPS_difference and SCRPS_se. Its attributes include reference, refit, and for each model n_observations, the number of observations with scores, n_failed, the number of failed test-set assessments, and binary, whether it is a model of binary outcomes.

Details

Lower is better for both scores, and a negative difference means a better score than that of the reference model. A PIT_area below PIT_area_limit is one that a correct model would give (see assess_prediction()). For a model of binary outcomes the area is not a check of calibration, so the print of the summary and to_table() show neither its area nor its limit. The print says why. The summary still has them.

An observation in several test sets is first given the average of its scores, so that it counts once. The scores of a model are then averaged over the observations. The differences from the reference are those of the observations that both models have scores for, and their standard error is the standard deviation of these differences divided by the square root of their number. It treats the observations as independent, so it is only approximate, and it is too small when the differences at neighbouring locations are alike.

The scores of each test set are in the scores element of the result of assess_prediction().

See also

assess_prediction(), and to_table() for a table to render.
